question: How will the peak intensity and half width of the 12.6 ° characteristic peak of additives added to perovskite precursors to prepare thin films change in XRD characterization?
control: Systematic parameter adjustments underlie the fabrication of a perovskite cell that was constituted, capturing how controlled conditions influence a PCE of 15.61%, FF of 74.28%, Voc of 1.0118 V, and Jsc of 20.77 mA/cm². The core perovskite solution, composed of Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1 at 1.73 mol/L, served as the foundational matrix for the solar cell. For the SAM solution, Me-4PACz (0.33 mg/mL) was added to the previous solution. And chlorinated MACl under 2.5 mg/mL concentration in the perovskite precursor solution. The prepared precursor solution was spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s onto the substrate. In the last 6 s of the second step, the anti-solvent (160 µL of chlorobenzene) was dropped in the center at a constant rate The substrates were sequentially heated at 110 °C for 25 min for perovskite crystal formation. XRD analysis showed a diffraction peak was identified at around 12.65°, with an intensity of 2107.567622 cts and a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 0.207035042, which corresponds to the characteristic peak of PbI2. The relatively low intensity of this peak suggests a limited presence of residual PbI2.
target: Through deliberate control of solution composition, coating speeds, and thermal treatments, this perovskite cell was prepared, leading to a PCE of 17.52%, a fill factor of 71.52%, a Voc of 1.05228 V, and a Jsc of 23.29 mA/cm². A perovskite precursor featuring Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1 at 1.73 mol/L was prepared to initiate the fabrication process. Mixed SAMs solution, consisting of MeO-2PACz (0.2475 mg/mL) and DMACPA (0.0825 mg/mL) in ethanol were prepared. To prepare the precursor solutions with MACl (7.0 mg/mL) and PEAI (0.8 mg/mL), the additive were added to the precursor solution. For the perovskite deposition process, the perovskite films were deposited using a two-step spin-coating process at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. A total of 160 µL of CB was dripped onto the center of film at 6 s before the end of spin-coating. The resulting wet perovskite films were annealed at 110 °C for 25 min. XRD analysis showed a diffraction peak was identified at around 12.65°, with an intensity of 277.8755447 cts and a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 0.277305425, which corresponds to the characteristic peak of PbI2. The relatively low intensity of this peak suggests a limited presence of residual PbI2.
